findings.where: First screen, Mark's heading 'In my view, we are at a turning point in the story of public-private partnerships.'
findings.fault: The heading claims there is a turning point but never says what it is. Nothing on the first screen explains it or links to where Mark argues it: the supporting line goes on to describe his services instead. The line is from a 2020 blog post and appears here with no date, so in 2026 'a turning point' reads as a general commentator's opener rather than a view only he holds.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank staff member arriving from LinkedIn. They are shown an opinion but no argument, so the strongest line on the page doesn't prove his judgement and can't be followed up. The founder may object too: the personal-advisor test asks for his voice, not a line any PPP pundit could have written.

findings.where: Phone first screen: the order of photo, heading, address strip, then 'I advise multilateral development banks…'
findings.fault: On a phone, the only line that says what Mark does and for whom comes after the address strip and below the first screen. A phone visitor is asked to write to him before being told what he offers. All they have to go on is the small credential under his name.
findings.who_objects: A bank or agency officer opening the link on a phone. They fail the 5-second test (what is this, is it for me) and reach the email address with no reason yet to use it.

findings.where: Article page specimen: the byline 'Mark Moseley · MMM Infra Blog No. 8 · 18 September 2024' and the end of the article
findings.fault: The article page has no one-line bio and no contact address. A reader who lands on the article straight from a shared post sees only a name and a blog number. Nothing tells them who Mark is, and they have no way to write to him once the article has persuaded them.
findings.who_objects: A reader sent to the article from a LinkedIn post, the most likely way in for this audience. The page that does the most to win them over has no route to the one action.

findings.where: Article page specimen, Download row: 'Streamlining the PPP Process… Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF'
findings.fault: The newest talk is listed with no venue or host, so it says nothing about who asked him to speak. The link is also offered as a bare PDF download instead of leading to a page about the talk.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader judging standing by who asked for the work. A lecture with no venue can't be checked and proves nothing, and opening a PDF straight away hides what it is before they commit to it.

findings.where: First screen as a whole: the identity line, the supporting line and the address strip
findings.fault: Nothing on the first screen says where he has worked (regions or countries) or which bodies have used his advice. Apart from the World Bank credential there is no proof of work. A visitor can't tell whether he has worked in their region or for an institution like theirs.
findings.who_objects: Staff at a regional development bank or agency, who choose advisors by project type and region. 'Have you done this here, for people like us' is the first thing they need to be sure of before writing.

findings.fault: The navigation has no Contact item. Once the visitor has scrolled past the hero's address strip, or is on any other page, the menu offers no labelled way to reach him.
findings.who_objects: A returning visitor who has decided to get in touch and looks in the menu for how. They have to scroll back to the top or hunt for the address.
